newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Meditrust deal may add to EPS in 98.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Meditrust deal may add to EPS in 98.

text.p: Meditrust SBI's merger with Santa Anita Cos could be accretive to earnings as soon as next year, Meditrust chairman and chief executive Abraham Gosman said on Monday.
"At it's inception, it will be dilutive," Gosman told Reuters in an interview. "Next year, it should be neutral to accretive...it could (add) five to six percent to earnings per share.

Meditrust, a real estate investment trust specializing in long-term care facilities and rehabilitation hospitals, earned $3.01 per share in 1996. According to First Call, analysts expected Meditrust to earn $3.14 this year.
Santa Anita earned $0.68 in 1996, and the First Call consensus was $0.69.
The new company will pursue acquisitions, especially in the retirement housing and healthcare sectors. "We'll be acquiring on a national basis, not specific to a particular region," Gosman said.
Gosman said the company currently has a $280 million revolving line of credit that can be expanded to $400 million.
He expected that within the next two years, the company may be able to raise $1 billion in common stock equity on the market, and would have another $1 billion in available debt.
Gosman said he expected that the consolidation of the REIT industry to accelerate. "You'll continue to see consolidation in the REIT industry," Gosman said.
On Sunday, Meditrust and Santa Anita Cos, a paired-share REIT, said they signed a deal for a tax-free exchange of shares.
Under terms, Santa Anita shareholders have the option to receive cash at $31.00 per share for up to 3.2 million of their Santa Anita shares.
Under the definitive agreement, Meditrust will be merged into Santa Anita through a reverse merger.
A "paired-share" ownership structure pairs the shares of an operating company and a REIT together on a one-for-one basis with the shares trading as a unit.
Santa Anita, which owns and operates the California race track, is one of only a handful of REITs in the U.S. that are permitted through a grandfathered clause to both own and operate facilities.
Meditrust shares fell 1-1/2 to 35-7/8. Santa Anita stock rose 1-7/8 to 29-1/4.
